incident.headline: The peninsula remains evacuated; the fire is still progressing and not controlled.
incident.summary: The operational picture remains critical and has broadened beyond the peninsula: Reuters reports the prefecture’s 14:00 briefing put the fire at more than 12,500 hectares and 44,000 evacuations over 48 hours. About 1,000 firefighters are deployed; 53 homes and a campsite have been destroyed. Reuters also lists Arès and Andernos among the communes under preventive evacuation; navigation on Arcachon Bay is temporarily prohibited. There is no signal that travelling to Cap Ferret is viable.

currentAssessment.verdict: Do not travel to Cap Ferret: the whole peninsula remains evacuated and the fire is still progressing.
currentAssessment.narrative: The decisive facts are the complete evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula, a fire still described as uncontrolled and advancing, and the expanded emergency response. Reuters reports the prefecture’s 14:00 briefing put the fire at more than 12,500 hectares and 44,000 evacuations over 48 hours; about 1,000 firefighters are engaged. Authorities report 53 homes and a campsite destroyed. Injury reporting conflicts: the earlier prefectural/SDIS briefing reported 27 firefighters treated, six hospitalised, while a later local report gives a higher figure that is not independently corroborated. Reuters also lists Arès and Andernos for preventive evacuation, and the maritime prefecture has temporarily prohibited navigation on Arcachon Bay. Inbound road access remains closed to the public.
currentAssessment.confidence: High confidence on the evacuation and navigation restrictions, the approximately 1,000-firefighter deployment, the prefecture-attributed 12,500-hectare / 44,000-evacuation update, and the absence of a viable travel signal. The clearest corroborated damage count remains 53 homes and one campsite destroyed, with 2,000 homes saved. Treat the conflicting later firefighter-injury count as unconfirmed; earlier wording that 80 homes were burned or affected should not be read as 80 confirmed total destructions.
priorities: The entire peninsula remains evacuated; Reuters also lists Arès and Andernos for preventive evacuation on the northern side of the bay.
The fire remains uncontrolled; 27 firefighters have required treatment and forecast westerly gusts could reach 80 km/h.
Road entry and ordinary navigation on Arcachon Bay are unavailable, so there is no viable land or public-water route for a holiday trip.
The next meaningful threshold is official control of the fire and permission to enter, followed by road, ferry, utility, beach, business and forest-access reopening.

materialUpdates.title: Reuters attributes 12,500 hectares and 44,000 evacuations to the prefecture’s 14:00 briefing
materialUpdates.detail: Reuters’ later version says the Gironde prefecture’s 14:00 situation update put the still-uncontrolled Saumos fire at more than 12,500 hectares. It reports 44,000 evacuations over 48 hours, alongside about 1,000 firefighters, more than 260 ground vehicles, 53 homes and one campsite destroyed; it also lists Arès and Andernos for preventive evacuation. The evacuation and Arcachon Bay navigation restrictions remain operative; this confirmation does not establish a reopening.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: The higher 12,500-hectare and 44,000-evacuation totals are now attributed by Reuters to the prefecture’s 14:00 briefing, rather than standing only as a local-media report. Its later version also adds Andernos to the reported preventive-evacuation scope. No access or reopening change follows.

sources.name: Reuters reporting the Gironde prefecture’s 14:00 situation briefing
Mairie de Lège-Cap-Ferret incident notice (evacuation remains the operative authority instruction)

materialUpdates.title: Midday briefing confirms a larger response, firefighter injuries and extensive property loss
materialUpdates.detail: The latest prefectural and emergency-service briefing puts about 1,000 firefighters on the Gironde fire. Authorities report 53 homes and one campsite destroyed, 2,000 homes saved, and 27 firefighters treated, including six taken to hospital; no deaths have been reported. The SDIS says the fire advanced at 800–1,000 hectares per hour for several hours overnight, while forecast westerly gusts of up to 80 km/h remain a concern.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: The response has risen from about 800 to about 1,000 firefighters. The clearest official damage and injury assessment is now 53 homes and one campsite destroyed, 27 firefighters treated and six hospitalised, with no deaths reported.

sources.name: AFP reporting the midday prefectural and SDIS briefing

materialUpdates.title: Evacuation expands to Arès and ordinary navigation is prohibited on Arcachon Bay
materialUpdates.detail: Reuters reports that the prefecture ordered a mandatory preventive evacuation in Arès and that the maritime prefecture imposed a temporary navigation ban on Arcachon Bay. The restriction confirms that a listed ferry timetable cannot be treated as an available public route to Cap Ferret.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: The disruption has expanded beyond the peninsula: Arès is under mandatory evacuation and ordinary navigation on the bay is temporarily prohibited.

sources.name: Reuters reporting the prefectural and maritime measures

materialUpdates.title: Interior Minister reports more than 10,000 hectares burned and about 40,000 evacuations
materialUpdates.detail: At Friday morning's national briefing, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the Saumos fire had passed 10,000 hectares and led to about 40,000 evacuations; he also said it was not under control and was continuing to progress. AFP later reported 80 homes burned, including about 50 destroyed, so the dashboard does not treat all 80 as confirmed total losses. This is a later, materially higher assessment than overnight prefecture-based reporting.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: The best later public briefing raises the reported footprint above 10,000 hectares and puts evacuations at about 40,000; the fire was still progressing and not controlled. Later reporting distinguishes 80 homes burned or affected from about 50 destroyed.

sources.name: Public Sénat reporting the Interior Minister briefing
AFP reporting the later property-loss clarification

materialUpdates.title: The affected area has nearly doubled and the fire remains uncontrolled
materialUpdates.detail: Late Thursday the prefecture reported about 4,800 hectares affected. Friday-morning reporting based on the latest authority briefings moved first to 8,700 hectares and then towards 10,000 hectares. Civil Protection described the Saumos fire as the largest of the season and said it was not under control.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: The reported footprint moved from about 4,800 hectares to at least 8,700 and potentially 10,000; authorities still did not describe the fire as controlled.

materialUpdates.title: Evacuation extended to the entire Cap Ferret peninsula
materialUpdates.detail: The prefecture ordered the third and final evacuation phase, requiring everyone still present from Claouey to the tip of Cap Ferret to leave. The RD106 was designated as the road exit towards Bordeaux, with temporary maritime evacuation shuttles from Grand Piquey, Le Canon, Port de la Vigne and Bélisaire.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: Le Canon moved from a threatened location to an explicit evacuation zone, and maritime shuttles were added to the road evacuation.

materialUpdates.title: The fire breached a defensive containment line
materialUpdates.detail: The prefecture said the fire crossed a line established by firefighters at around 01:00. That breach triggered the rapid expansion of evacuation orders down the peninsula.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: A firefighting line failed at about 01:00, directly triggering the rapid extension of evacuation orders down the peninsula.

materialUpdates.title: Fire entered the built-up fringe of Lège and homes were lost
materialUpdates.detail: The prefecture described the fire as very active around Lège-Cap-Ferret, with roughly 4,800 hectares affected, several homes destroyed and close to 20,000 precautionary evacuations across the wider area.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: The incident crossed from forest into the built-up fringe: homes were destroyed and the approach to the peninsula was directly threatened.

materialUpdates.title: Normal peninsula activity began shutting down
materialUpdates.detail: The town hall closed all forest cycle paths, all three lifeguard stations and the lighthouse, and suspended commercial marine traffic. Entry on the RD106 was restricted while the initial evacuation expanded.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: Forest cycling, lifeguarded beaches, the lighthouse and commercial marine traffic all closed before the full evacuation order.

access.name: Travel to the peninsula
access.detail: The entire peninsula remains under an evacuation order. Public inbound travel is not permitted; road and maritime access are restricted to authorised evacuation, emergency and essential movements.

access.name: Road access to the peninsula
access.detail: Ordinary inbound road access to the peninsula has not reopened. Open for destination-by-destination status.

access.name: Road access · Claouey
access.detail: No authority has announced that ordinary inbound road access to Claouey has reopened. The evacuation order and peninsula access restrictions still apply.

access.name: Road access · Petit Piquey & Piraillan
access.detail: No authority has announced that ordinary inbound road access to Petit Piquey or Piraillan has reopened. The evacuation order and peninsula access restrictions still apply.

access.name: Road access · Grand Piquey
access.detail: No authority has announced that ordinary inbound road access to Grand Piquey has reopened. The evacuation order and peninsula access restrictions still apply.

access.name: Road access · Le Canon & L’Herbe
access.detail: No authority has announced that ordinary inbound road access to Le Canon or L’Herbe has reopened. The evacuation order and peninsula access restrictions still apply.

access.name: Road access · Cap Ferret
access.detail: No authority has announced that ordinary inbound road access to Cap Ferret village or Bélisaire has reopened. The evacuation order and peninsula access restrictions still apply.

access.name: Maritime leisure activities
access.detail: Surf schools, sailing schools, boat hire and other tourist-facing water activities cannot operate normally while the peninsula is evacuated and the public cannot enter.

access.name: Beaches
access.detail: Residents and visitors have been told to leave the area. Municipal lifeguard stations are closed.

access.name: Cycling & hiking
access.detail: All forest cycle paths are closed; Gironde remains at red-level wildfire risk.

localCommerce.name: Groceries and food shops
localCommerce.detail: The evacuation order prevents normal customer access. No general reopening of supermarkets, food shops or the Cap Ferret market has been announced.

localCommerce.name: Pharmacies
localCommerce.detail: No pharmacy-specific reopening or public-access arrangement has been found. Emergency and authority instructions take priority over normal listed hours.

localCommerce.name: Other local shops and services
localCommerce.detail: There is no general announcement that visitor-facing retail or everyday local services have resumed.

ferries.name: Arcachon ↔ Bélisaire ferry
ferries.detail: The maritime prefecture has temporarily prohibited navigation on Arcachon Bay. Emergency evacuation operations are distinct; the UBA timetable is not an available tourist or ordinary local route.

ferries.name: Emergency evacuation shuttles
ferries.detail: Authorities announced temporary evacuation boats from Grand Piquey, Le Canon, Port de la Vigne and Bélisaire. These are not evidence of normal passenger service.

ferries.name: Excursions and leisure boats
ferries.detail: The temporary navigation ban confirms that normal commercial excursions and leisure boating are unavailable.

socialSignals.title: A local-news post relayed evacuees’ accounts of the night the peninsula changed
socialSignals.summary: A Bluesky post from Rue89 Bordeaux linked accounts from Cécile, Evelyne and Pierre describing their overnight evacuation as the wildfire reached the peninsula.
socialSignals.interesting: It adds recent first-person evacuation texture from a local-news outlet without changing the official access or safety guidance.

socialSignals.title: A local-news post gave a close-range indication of the fire's proximity to homes
socialSignals.summary: A Bluesky post from a local journalist relayed reporting that the fire was about 150 metres from homes at Cap Ferret and described firefighters' concern about increasingly unpredictable fire behaviour as weather deteriorates.
socialSignals.interesting: It supplies a recent, concrete proximity detail and weather-related operational colour; it does not change the official evacuation, access or safety guidance.

socialSignals.title: A media-linked post described the peninsula as a ghost town as the last evacuees reached Arcachon
socialSignals.summary: A Bluesky news-flow post relayed reporting from the final evacuation arrivals in Arcachon and described the emptied peninsula as having the atmosphere of a ghost town.
socialSignals.interesting: It adds immediate human and visual colour to the completed evacuation without changing the official access status.

socialSignals.title: A coastal weather observer said the forecast wind shift was already under way
socialSignals.summary: A Mastodon post bridged into Bluesky reported that the coastal airflow had begun turning westerly near Biscarrosse, with north-westerly flow expected later.
socialSignals.interesting: The observation offers timely ground-level context for the wind change firefighters and authorities were already watching, but it is not an official forecast.

socialSignals.title: A news-flow post highlighted a gas-cylinder explosion captured during live television coverage
socialSignals.summary: The post relayed footage of a gas cylinder exploding in Lège-Cap-Ferret as a television crew prepared a live report.
socialSignals.interesting: It illustrates the secondary hazards facing crews around affected buildings; it does not establish a new perimeter or casualty count.

socialSignals.title: Road footage showed why the single land exit was a central concern
socialSignals.summary: A Reddit contributor linked recent footage attributed to Sud Ouest journalist Daniel Bozec from the peninsula road while commenters tracked whether it remained usable.
socialSignals.interesting: It adds visual, on-the-ground context to the otherwise abstract RD106 access status. Treat the timing and exact location as unverified.
socialSignals.source: X via r/france · Daniel Bozec / Sud Ouest

socialSignals.title: Commenters described ferries being requisitioned for evacuation to Arcachon
socialSignals.summary: Participants in the main r/france incident thread said the Cap Ferret–Arcachon ferries had been requisitioned and that sea evacuations were under way.
socialSignals.interesting: This supplies operational colour on how maritime evacuation functioned, while corroborating official reporting that boats supplemented the single road exit.

socialSignals.title: Local image post offered a resident-level view of the smoke and fire
socialSignals.summary: A user describing the incident as being near their home posted a small set of current images rather than another news link.
socialSignals.interesting: The post is useful as visual atmosphere and local perspective, not as evidence for perimeter, control status or safety decisions.

socialSignals.title: A cockpit video showed the intensity of a Canadair water pickup
socialSignals.summary: A Bluesky post shared an inside-the-aircraft view and explained the speed and lift needed when the aircraft makes contact with the water.
socialSignals.interesting: It does not establish how many aircraft are assigned locally, but it gives unusually concrete colour on the aerial operation being discussed around the fire.
